 LNPK Grocery opens, awaits USDA approval for SNAP benefits
 Fatima Avalos WDIO 
 --> 
 LNPK Grocery in Duluth opening soon with fresh produce stocked
 LNPK Grocery in Duluth is opening soon with fresh produce stocked from the Ecolibrium3's Urban farm at Lake Superior College. After months of delays and technical challenges, LNPK Grocery is now open, but there’s still one more hurdle left before it can fill the food access gap in the Lincoln Park neighborhood.
 The store faced construction and permitting setbacks that pushed back its planned summer 2025 opening. 
 “As you work on an old building and try to get it up to code for a grocery, you’re going to come across some challenges,” said Jacob Dillon, Manager of LNPK Grocery.
 Their mission is to supply the community with access to fresh, healthy, and accessible grocery options. The neighborhood has long struggled with food access, classified as a food desert with 41% of residents reporting barriers to getting food.
 “A lot of people, as they come in, they’re just grateful that they can walk like 15 minutes from their house to come get groceries. It’s much more convenient than going up the hill or driving to West Duluth when you just need a few things,” said Dillon.
 Since their soft opening, the community has been receptive and supportive.
 “Definitely just makes living in this area a little better,” said Dane Larson, who’s been living in Lincoln Park for three years.
 “Just being able to go walk or even a minute drive to pick up something while you’re cooking makes a big difference in kind of quality of life,” said Larson.
 However, the store is still waiting for final approval to accept SNAP benefits from the U.S. Department of Agriculture. They sent in an application to become a SNAP retailer in July, but haven’t heard received an update since then.
 “I feel this is probably a little longer than normal situations. Don’t really know what the holdup is, all of our stuff’s been in. We’ve resubmitted things, we’ve dotted all the I’s and crossed all the T’s,” said Dillon.
 He says the timeline of when LNPK Grocery can accept SNAP and WIC benefits is all dependent on the USDA. 
 “We hope it’s soon. I mean, we’re ready to go with it if we got approved tomorrow, but we’re patiently waiting just like everybody else.”
 LNPK Grocery is located at 2014 West Superior Street and is open Monday-Friday from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. A grand opening will be held once SNAP approval is received.
